Hero.title: Full stack developer turning business problems into software running in
Hero.description: I work end to end: web, mobile and desktop interfaces, APIs, databases, AI agents and integrations with payments, webhooks and real-time channels (WebSockets and SSE). I enjoy solving real problems with maintainable software and solid architecture.

Experience.label: 01 — Experience
Experience.title: Software running in production, for real companies.
Experience.subtitle: Almost four years building SaaS, mobile apps and payment integrations.

infoluckCurrent.description: Building SaaS products for food service: a WhatsApp AI assistant (Electron, Node.js and Gemini), a digital menu with real-time Pix payment confirmation, the next-generation ERP (React and Go) and Flutter kiosk and KDS apps. I set up projects from scratch, build CI/CD pipelines with Docker and review Pull Requests.

build.description: Maintenance and new features for restaurant SaaS applications. Built a logistics feature with delivery zones drawn as polygons on Google Maps, replacing straight-line distance pricing, and a debounced Google Places autocomplete that cut billable requests by about 80%. Payments with Pix, Stripe, Google Pay and Apple Pay; real-time waiter calls over WebSockets; QR Code table ordering. React Native apps for tablets, self-service kiosk, KDS and POS terminals integrated with PagBank and Stone.

infoluckWeb.description: Built MenuLuck 2.0, which moved the digital menu to React. Designed and built front-ends with Figma, React and TypeScript. Maintained legacy PHP, jQuery and Delphi systems backed by PostgreSQL, including procedures and reports.

infoluckIt.description: Support for ERP, POS and SaaS systems, investigating issues with SQL/PostgreSQL. Infrastructure, servers, printers, training and reports. Moved to the development team after independently solving complex technical issues.

Experience.before: Before IT: assembly, calibration and repair of electronic equipment at IBRAMED Brasil.

Projects.label: 02 — Projects
Projects.title: Real products, from AI agents to logistics.

infoluckWeb.description: Business management SaaS with sales, finance, inventory, reports and product catalog modules. React and TypeScript front-end built from Figma prototypes.

menuluck.description: Multi-tenant digital menu with delivery, QR Code table service and self-service. I built version 2.0 in React and remain its main developer: Pix confirmed in real time over SSE, scheduled orders, combos, per-merchant GA4 and Docker CI/CD.

lrStore.description: Mobile electronics store with Stripe payments.

portal.description: Portal where the accountants of Infoluck's clients run tax analysis and queries with charts and reports.

agentLuck.description: AI customer-service assistant for restaurants on WhatsApp, built solo. An Electron desktop app with WhatsApp Web embedded and a multi-tenant Node.js back-end with Gemini and an OpenAI fallback. It batches back-to-back messages into one call, hands off to a human on request and controls cost with prompt caching and per-store token caps. Redis for idempotency and distributed locks, real-time orders over SSE, auto-update and Sentry.

infoluckErp.description: Infoluck's next-generation ERP. I set up the front-end from scratch (ports & adapters, mock-first, Vitest, CI/CD) and built cash register, finance and product composition, with in-browser image background removal via WebAssembly. On the Go API: permissions and modules gated by company type.

timerRodeo.description: Official bull-riding timer that streams the clock to the arena scoreboard over WebSocket every 50 ms, with timer-drift correction, backoff reconnection and 47 tests, including golden tests.

kiosk.description: Self-service apps I built and maintained at Build Solutions and Infoluck: a kiosk with card-terminal payment, a kitchen display (KDS) refreshed over WebSocket and an order-number board for customers.

deliveryZones.description: Delivery zones drawn as polygons by the merchant, replacing straight-line pricing that got fees wrong across hills and highways. A custom debounced Google Places autocomplete cut billable requests by about 80%.
